context: Alfira is a young tiefling bard who was apprenticed to Lihala, who died horribly in a gnoll attack; Alfira is struggling to compose and perform a quiet memorial song for her lost teacher. In the grove she’s playing lute as a soft, emotional moment, but nearby small animals (a bird and a squirrel among them) are loudly dramatic and mocking, trying to drown out or parody her music. The camera pans from Alfira to the critters, whose over-the-top complaints and duet steal the scene and force the player to respond. The player can comfort or assist Alfira, tell the animals to be quiet or egg them on to sing along, and — if the song is completed with help — Alfira can stand and finish it in a cinematic.
